title: Systolic alarm reaction did not establish incremental albuminuria prediction across two NHANES cycles
abstract: We trained fixed logistic models in 4,923 NHANES 2015–2016 adults and tested them without refitting in 4,369 adults in the separate 2017–2018 survey sample. Adding first-minus-third systolic blood pressure to conventional risk factors, mean blood pressure and within-visit standard deviations changed examination-weighted log loss by -0.00006935 (conditional stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval -0.00027532 to 0.00013723). AUROC changed from 0.708821 to 0.708969; source-cycle out-of-fold performance worsened. The prespecified improvement criterion failed. The outcome is single-sample albuminuria, not chronic kidney disease. Separate survey cycles provide external-sample validation but share survey infrastructure and lack definitive cross-cycle person linkage. Author self-checks reconstructed urine ratios and prediction scores, and offline clean reruns matched exactly. No clinical, causal, equivalence or independent-institution validation claim is made.
